restrictions: Target sha256-r37-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..36 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is verified with the target before it is returned.

Algorithm: the two-block attack of Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian and Zhu (IACR ePrint 2026/1120) with its 37-step characteristic and the Step-1 solution S as transcribed in 6c77089c, the 222 largest classes of A0-variants of S (782,800 variants; 1c368173, b947b377, 1f12a09a), each class base | s for s in one of ten lists whose free bits 0, 2, 3 (or 0) form a cube, and the packed good-pair stage of 0db0eeb6; as in ffbe30bb the eight value bits E18[1,5,10,11,18,28,29], E19[29] are not imposed (four patterns, proof.md Section 7.6); new here (R16x), E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] are not imposed (proof.md Section 7.4c). No table is indexed by x = A_{-1} and no row-16 mask table is used: per first block a bit-sliced W7 test of the 222 classes, per passing class bit-sliced W6 tests of the reps of its list in at most 8 runs, an immediate four-entry streaming group register (no retained good-pair collection), the packed row-16 address, two 4096-word chunk tables and an exact test, then rows 16..36.

Cost: revised caps N_FB = 60955086511892727 first blocks (each one target compression plus 603 counted fixed operations) and V_MAX = 2731474318523820346781 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded), with A_C = 2^60 (characteristic and SFS-pair search), A_S = 2^50 (Step-1 SAT solve), DEV = 2^40 (development), PRE = 2^38 ordinary operations, FIN = 1600 operations, six verification compressions and a 94072423077-operation cap overshoot (proof.md A3): T = 5980699729439825520979 / 2644 target compressions on every run, claimed time_log2 60.97230 rounded upward. Every target compression is charged one unit; every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition (address additions included), comparison and branch is one primitive, the plane programs counted by an algebra with static constants and inversion flags (proof.md Section 9.1); there is no decision-DAG pricing. The 13-bit shared scan table and pruned circuit planes optimize costs (proof.md A1-A3).

Success probability at least 0.39 (0.390000002371393 under the stated premises) under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-71.47 with the four row-18/19 value patterns and R16x (E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] not imposed) accepted jointly: the lower, rounded down to two decimals, of the one-sided 99 percent bounds 2^-71.4629 and 2^-71.4524 of two preregistered blocks of 128 replicates of a sequential Monte-Carlo estimator written for the baseline filing, proof.md Section 7.4c and Appendix G; the same program with Table 15 cells reproduces the registered study of 7319bba), H3 (given one success, at most 2^-9.4 further successes expected in the same first block) and H7, by a per-first-block Bonferroni bound and independence across first blocks. With revised N_FB and V_MAX, Chebyshev bounds work-cap overflow below 0.00057796 (proof.md A3). No expected-work bound and no independence-of-conditions model is used. Historical studies are inherited.

Memory: all tables, the code, constants and the separate 256-byte fill/control reserve occupy at most 796768 bytes < 2^19.62 < 2^20 (proof.md A4). The 796768-byte total accounts for the 262144-byte 13-bit scan table and 86 resident z_planes words (pruning 10 words of unread broadcast planes); the old table is not retained. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score. The per-first-block counts of the ledger are exact expectations or stated bounds on them (proof.md Section 11.1 and A3); the simulation of proof.md Section 13.3 on real first blocks is a check and is not used in the ledger.

heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings; their chaining values CV1 = F_37(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values; in particular x = A_{-1} is uniform on 2^32 and independent of cb = C6 - A_{-2}, which is uniform on 2^32. Consequences used: each of the 222 classes passes the W7 test with probability p7 = |F7|/2^32 exactly, each variant of a passing class then passes F6 with probability p6 = |F6|/2^32 exactly, and given both, W0..W5 are uniform and independent of (W6, W7) (proof.md Lemma 5.1); hence the expected number of good pairs per first block is g = 782,800 p7 p6 = 830.988, the expected counts of the ledger, and the independence of distinct first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected numbers of passing classes, good pairs, survivors and row-16 passes per first block; the expected operation count of the counted program; the law of the second-block words that defines q3; independence across first blocks (proof.md Section 10). Not the validity of any output: every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured by 7319bba with the attack's own filters on real first blocks in C (2^21 and 2^23 first blocks: passing classes 7,400,134 and 29,545,568 against 7,388,160 and 29,552,640 expected; good pairs ratio 1.0034 and 1.0011; row-16 pairs z = +0.88, +0.51), and by this filing's simulation of the counted program on 50,000 real first blocks (passing classes per first block 3.529 against the exact 3.523, good pairs 835.0 against 831.0, mean counted operations 46965 against the ledger's 46685). These are at most 2^23 real first blocks, not 2^58.3; the organizer experiment a0-online-r37 checks functional exactness only and is not evidence for H1.
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on at most 2^23 first blocks. The class tests of one first block are strongly correlated (their c7 values are close), so per-first-block counts are overdispersed; only their expectations and the independence across first blocks are used. The class test uses the single word x, so H1 is also an assumption about that word of the digest of a 37-step compression. Historical experiments and studies are baseline-author evidence, not fresh measurements of this revision.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 782,800 variants of the 222 classes (each equally likely, as examined here) and the 32 elements of L* of Pr[rows 16..36 of both members follow every cell and every printed two-bit condition closing at rows >= 16 (corrected reading A15[29] = A17[29]), the eight value bits E18[1,5,10,11,18,28,29] and E19[29] of Table 15 not imposed, and (R16x) E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] not imposed: exactly the cells and conditions of experiments/lowm.py] satisfies q3_used = 2^-71.47 <= q3 <= 2^-70, where 2^-71.47 is the lower, rounded down to two decimals of log2, of the one-sided 99 percent Student lower bounds (2^-71.4629 and 2^-71.4524) of the means of two preregistered blocks of 128 replicates (NP = 8192) of a sequential Monte-Carlo estimator written for this filing (Appendices F and G), run on exactly this family with both relaxations as one carrier.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g 32 q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10). The good pairs and the later rows are those of 7319bba; this filing changes how the good pairs are found, not which pairs are good, and which pairs count as a success: (from ffbe30bb) the value patterns of rows 18 and 19 and (new) R16x at rows 16 and 17, which also gives the four l = 0, 2, 16, 18 row-16 values.
heuristics.extrapolation: Lemma 7.1: rows 16..22 have exactly the same probability for every variant; a variant enters rows >= 23 only through W8 in W23 and W24, so only the four W24 conditions can depend on it (about 2^-4 for every W8x). Our estimator (exact row 16, exact importance weights at rows 17..21, (W6, W7) uniform on F6 x F7, W8 drawn uniformly from the 782,800 variants; Appendix F) was preregistered (validation V with Table 15 cells: mean 2^-73.9911, bound 2^-74.0064, z = +0.66 against the registered study B of 7319bba, mean 2^-73.9987, bound 2^-74.0225, validation PASSES both preregistered criteria (|z| <= 2.576; bound within 0.04 of -74.0225); main blocks R1 and R2 with the eight value characters of the two E cells removed: means 2^-71.9975 and 2^-71.9868, relative sd 0.0714 and 0.0681, bounds 2^-72.0191 and 2^-72.0074, declared 2^-72.02; stage factors of rows 18, 19 and 21 -8.00, -10.00 and -2.00 bits against -15.00, -6.00 and -1.00 for Table 15, structural gain 2.00) and again with R16x (constants written from the counted program; the same binary reproduces the four-pattern outputs byte for byte; joint blocks J1 and J2: means 2^-71.4296 and 2^-71.4177, relative sd 0.1096 and 0.1143, bounds 2^-71.4629 and 2^-71.4524, 0.55 bits above the four patterns alone; our earlier full-path test of R16x with independent rehash of all 30,814 collisions gave +0.590 bit [0.548, 0.631]). The four-pattern relaxation (exactly four feasible patterns, three verified further collisions) is ffbe30bb's; here the three collisions are re-checked against this package's cells. R16x is ours (each of its two conditions alone is necessary; a sweep of 30 further condition pairs found no further gain). Here the examined law is the studied law (every variant of every passing class, no weighting), so no hedge is added. With q3 one bit lower the claim would be 61.57158, with the four patterns alone (2^-72.02) 61.28957 and with the Table 15 value 2^-74.03 62.76763.
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo bound, not a theorem; its coverage rests on the approximate normality of the mean of 128 replicates (relative sd 0.1096 and 0.1143, about twice the Table 15 study's because few children survive the row-19 stage); row-22 survivors are heavily duplicated within a replicate; the row-22 stage draws (W6, W7) uniformly from F6 x F7, which is argued, not measured; depends on the reading of the '+' cells. The estimator is ours and was validated against the registered study, not against a second independent implementation. The count of four patterns is a solver enumeration (Bitwuzla; Z3 on smaller cases) for the published dense part with the signed cells of rows 14 and 15 kept (with rows 12..15 removed as well it admits 128 patterns); other dense parts were not explored, and our estimator does not use the solver. R16x has no solver enumeration: its value rests on the estimator and on our full-path test with rehashed collisions; patterns of rows 16..21 outside the program's cells (for example the E18 XOR pattern {24,23,16,15}) are not counted. No organizer experiment estimates q3. A stated premise, not an established fact. Historical experiments and studies are baseline-author evidence, not fresh measurements of this revision.

heuristics.statement: For every trial t = (first block, variant, l), the expected number of other successful trials of the same first block given that t succeeds is at most 2^-9.4: E[X_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-9.4. Equivalently: (a) the expected number of other l in L* succeeding with the same variant is at most 2^-11, and (b) for other good pairs t' of the same first block, Pr[t' succeeds | t succeeds, t' good] <= 2^35 Pr[t' succeeds | t' good].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= (1 - 2^-10.4) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10). The good pairs of a first block and their dependence structure are those of 7319bba; this filing changes the order in which they are processed, not the set.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) 7319bba's replay of 19,620,436 distinct Step-3 successes of the SMC: rebuilding W0..W5 and testing the other 31 elements of L* through rows 14..36 gave 0 further successes (rule-of-three 95 percent bound 2^-22.65 per success; the accepted patterns raise the chance of passing rows 18 and 19 by about 4 and R16x the chance of the whole path by about 1.6, with four more l holding row 16, so about 2^-19.8, far below 2^-11; in that replay the other l fail at row 16 or 17). (b) With q3 <= 2^-70 (H2; it holds for 2^-71.47), the expected number of further successes among other good pairs is at most rho x N_good x 32 x q3 with N_good <= 782,800 (all variants of the family): 2^35 x 2^19.58 x 2^5 x 2^-70 = 2^-10.42, so delta <= 2^-11 + 2^-10.42 < 2^-9.4; the measured factor at the row-16 level over 2^21 and 2^23 real first blocks is 0.98 and 1.00. This is the bound of the earlier filings on this family; the whole family G would give 2^-6.5 and is not used.
heuristics.limitations: Rows >= 17 of distinct good pairs cannot be measured jointly within one first block; the premise leaves a margin of 2^35 over the measured row-16 factor, and the margin over the number of examined pairs is thin (delta <= 2^-9.68 against 2^-9.4). The replay samples are correlated through SMC resampling. A stated premise, not an established fact. Historical experiments and studies are baseline-author evidence, not fresh measurements of this revision.

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions, the SFS pair's inner values S and L* are used as advice. Their construction is charged A_S = 2^50 (the Step-1 SAT solve, reported by the paper at 2^41.3, and the completion of a Step-1 solution to the SFS pair) and A_C = 2^60 (the unpublished characteristic search); all development computation at DEV = 2^40. The variant family, the 222 class descriptors (below 2^13 bytes), the lists, the filter sets, L* and the tables are recomputed in the preprocessing (2^38 operations bound, itemised in proof.md Section 14.2).
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (2^60.00141) and the advice (below 2^13 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 11.2. A_S: 2^8.7 times the paper's reported Step-1 cost; the completion of a Step-1 solution to a full 37-step semi-free-start pair is reproduced in this package in about 25 milliseconds per pair (organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37). A_C: at the CPU-second price calibrated in the accepted filing 6eeefb64 (2^21.427 units at C = 2644 per solver CPU-second), 2^60 units is 2^38.57 CPU-seconds, 688,000 times the 593,858 CPU-seconds that filing charged as a measured complete re-run of the predecessor 35-step search. The same allowances are charged by the accepted filings on this track.
heuristics.limitations: The 37-step characteristic search time is unpublished; A_C is a bound by comparison with the accepted measurement of the predecessor search, not a measurement of this one. A_C = 2^56 would give 63.09331. Historical experiments and studies are baseline-author evidence, not fresh measurements of this revision.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 a word-RAM program of 256-bit primitives in which every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition, comparison, branch and jump is one primitive is charged by the primitives it executes. The W7 class test (166 primitives for all 222 classes) and the reordered batch-specialized W6 test of at most 256 reps (338 to 410 primitives, and 86 to 96 for each subtraction run) are straight-line plane programs whose counts do not depend on the data, produced by a plane algebra in which static constants fold and complemented planes carry an inversion flag at no cost, and in which a NOT is paid when an AND or OR meets unequal flags; two batches are processed together bit by bit with at most 20 live planes each (64 registers, no spill). Six fixed preprocessing orders preserve every finite list while exposing batch constants. Exhaustive construction asserts the exact zero- and one-plane tuples of every (list ID, batch) over its real lanes before 160 zero and 75 one plane words are omitted; the 100 W6 and 98 subtraction programs are measured and charged by their exact batch keys. The submitted attack path streams each gathered member directly into one four-entry group register and consumes every full group immediately; it allocates neither the predecessor's unbounded `mems` list nor its uncharged `goodset`. The group of four members is 31 primitives, the probe of a lane 11 or 12, the exact row-16 test 34, with the scalar and control items of proof.md Section 9. All tables, the code (bounded by 2^16 bytes) and the constants occupy 796,768 bytes = 2^19.62, below 2^20 bytes. The 222 classes are base | s for s in ten lists (computed, checked for all 782,800 variants); a list is the union of 2^|B| translates of its reps by the cube B of free bits {0, 2, 3} or {0}, and W6x does not depend on a cube bit s_b when q_b = 1 (Lemma 8.2: proved from the constants of S and checked), which the program uses to run only the main combination and subtract the constants of the other 2^|Q0| - 1 combinations that matter. This revision uses a single 8192-word 13-bit scan table with five chunks per 64-bit part; SCAN_FIX=58 and FIXED=603, as detailed in A1-A4. All other stage primitives are inherited.
heuristics.scope: The class-test, W6, scan, gather, group, probe and survivor terms of the ledger (essentially all of the 44800.33 data-dependent operations per first block), the fixed terms, the memory figure and the preprocessing bound (2^38 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: The program is experiments/lowm.py (the plane programs assert their counts at every execution; process_cv counts every scalar item where it executes; its attack mode retains at most four gathered entries and one successful candidate, while only explicit checker mode creates a brute-force goodset; the realized operation count of every category equals its closed formula on 50,000 simulated first blocks). It is exact against the scalar definitions: every lane of every class-test plane and every pass plane equals the F7 or F6 test of its definition (44,400 and 42,972 lanes in selftest, and every lane of every processed class in a0-online-r37), the sets of good pairs (all members, after the expansion of the reps) equal the brute-force sets, the address u equals W0 + s0(W1) from the step equations, the exact row-16 test equals the exhaustive enumeration of 2,097,152 pairs on all 32 l under the row-16 parity relaxation (Appendix A) and the generic row check on random and near-miss values, and the table stage never rejects a member.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited for the plane algebra (static constants and inversion flags are compile-time facts of the text; the W6 programs have 81 to 82 inversion flips that cost nothing because XORs absorb them and AND/OR of equally flagged planes use De Morgan; pricing every one of them as a NOT would give 61.01195) or for the register argument, which is a count of live planes, not a register allocation. The code size is a bound (at most 8192 primitives of at most 8 bytes). Branch pricing follows the earlier filings (a branch on a register is one primitive). The predecessor fatal finding lane_cost/F-COST-1 is addressed by making the submitted attack path perform the proof's immediate four-entry streaming; audit-only checker storage is excluded from the attack claim. The ceiling of the group count and the survivor scan are charged at their worst case (below 0.2 percent of the data-dependent work). Historical experiments and studies are baseline-author evidence, not fresh measurements of this revision.

heuristics.statement: The success floor is at least 0.39 for the revised physical-work cap. With inherited q3 >= 2^-71.47, g=435677125/524288 and s=2^-12, choose N_FB=60955086511892727, V_MAX=2731474318523820346781, mu0=0.49561105 and Pcap_assumed=0.00057796. The current vmax_fb/(s^2*N_FB*vbar) is below Pcap_assumed, and 1-exp(-(1-2^-10.4)*mu0)-Pcap_assumed-2^-60 = 0.390000002371393... > 0.39. The A3 ledger includes cap overshoot, preprocessing, advice, development and final verification; the current source checks the upward fifth-decimal bound using integer powers.
heuristics.scope: The current first-block budget and physical-work cap, total time and probability floor in A3; historical baseline cap numbers are overridden.
heuristics.extrapolation: The same base first-block independence and within-block dependence premises are inherited. Only deterministic scan, circuit and plane-load costs change; the current expected work, cap failure allowance, mu0 and first-block budget are recomputed.
heuristics.limitations: The 0.39 floor is the organizer's success requirement; the equation makes the success arithmetic exact rather than adding slack. Historical experiments and studies are baseline-author evidence, not fresh measurements of this revision.
